solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mortals try being transported over water like these six

indicators.note: in this clue the shuffled letters sit over, that is around, the word for water
transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters of the first two words are carried into a new order

parts.note: a puddle is a small pool of water

explanation.surface: A grim remark about the fate of six men shipped overseas, with mortal suffering carried across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being transported' signals the anagram and 'over' the wrapping. The six Dorset farm labourers were transported to Australia in 1834 for forming a trade union, so the wordplay doubles as their story.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the six Dorset trade unionists of 1834, so 'these six' points straight at the group.

clue.text: Set fire to church on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the hill comes first

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone sets light to a chapel on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something alight is to put a flame to it, a synonym of the verb meaning ignite deliberately.

clue.text: Fabulous member's finish to a line

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body; the 's is the link 'has'
an end is a finish
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Praise for a club member who finishes a line of verse superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabulous belongs to fable or legend, so it is mythically famous.

clue.text: False international body backed German air without pity

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an international body

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for pity sits inside the reversed German word
backed means the German word for air is written going back, from its end

parts.note: Luft is the German word for air
ruth is an old word for pity, surviving in ruthless

explanation.surface: An accusation that a body like the UN turned its back on German air without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' signals reversing the German word, and 'without' here means outside, not lacking, so it is a container signal. Ruth for pity survives mainly in 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A false statement is one lacking honesty, a direct synonym for lying.

clue.text: Abandon hope of being wrongly praised

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters of the last word are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone gives up hope because they have been praised for the wrong thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is a verb synonym for giving up hope entirely.

clue.text: Cover … letter, for example?

parts.note: the clue hints at a verb for wrapping, as when a paper case is wrapped around a letter; the ellipsis invites reading 'cover letter'

explanation.surface: A query about a cover letter, the note sent with a job application.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis tempts a reading of 'cover letter'. In fact the verb means to cover, and the paper cover a letter goes in shares its spelling bar a final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap or enclose something completely is to cover it, which a paper sleeve does to a letter.

clue.text: Subject to illustration

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an illustration

explanation.surface: A note that something is subject to having an illustration added.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion is its theme, a straight synonym.

clue.text: See 12
Exert leverage reportedly to gain trophy

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for exerting leverage is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to prise is to force open with leverage

explanation.surface: Someone uses leverage to grab a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is an award won in competition, a synonym.

clue.text: Officer reads list

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
a table is a list of data set out in order

explanation.surface: A police officer reads out a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer of the lowest rank in Britain bears this title.

clue.text: PC title lets Berlin author hog show

indicators.note: show signals that the letters of the three words are displayed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone lets the writer from Berlin dominate the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is Privy Counsellor, not police constable or personal computer; 'lets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Privy Counsellors in Britain are styled with this honorific before their names.

clue.text: Excess energy in symbol of ruler

indicators.note: in places the excess and energy inside the word for symbol

parts.note: a sign is a symbol
over means in excess, as in 'over the limit'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Surplus energy shows in the emblem of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch with supreme authority is a sovereign, a synonym for ruler; it is also a gold coin.

clue.text: See 9
Abandoned entertainment to move away from Tories

parts.note: something abandoned has been gone away from and deserted
a performer's act on a variety bill is called by this word

explanation.surface: An abandoned show leads someone to quit the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: A variety act is a 'turn' in British usage. The definition is cryptic: the Tories are on the political right, so going the other way moves away from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories sit on the political right, so a swing to the opposite side moves away from them, a punning sense.

clue.text: We leave poet to cover performing sleuth in place of speculation

indicators.note: to cover means the shortened poet's name wraps round the next pieces
We leave means those two letters depart from the poet's name

parts.note: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan poet and dramatist
taken as written
on means performing, as an actor on stage
tec is slang short for detective, a sleuth

explanation.surface: A poet steps aside to stand in for an actor playing a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' signals the deletion and 'to cover' the container. Marlowe is also Raymond Chandler's private eye, a neat decoy beside 'sleuth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco resort is famous for its casino, a place where people gamble or speculate.

clue.text: Athlete Christopher seems more crudely self-assertive

definitions.meaning: Chris ..., Olympic steeplechase champion of 1956 and founder of the London Marathon
comparative of brash, meaning crudely bold

explanation.surface: An Olympic runner comes across as rather pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means loud and pushy, and adding -er makes the comparative; the athlete's surname is spelt the same.

clue.text: Consequence of gripe led into Nye's basis for the welfare state

indicators.note: into places the shuffled letters inside the minister's surname

parts.note: Aneurin 'Nye' Bevan was the Labour minister who founded the NHS

indicators.note: a consequence is what results, so the letters result in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint pushed into Bevan's thinking became the foundation of the welfare state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consequence of' signals the anagram and 'into' the insertion. William Beveridge's 1942 report underpinned the postwar welfare state that Nye Bevan's NHS was part of.
explanation.definitionFit: Beveridge's 1942 report set out the scheme on which Britain's postwar welfare state was founded.

clue.text: Maxim for part of speech

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A grammar question about whether a saying counts as a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short pithy saying, a synonym for a traditional saw.

clue.text: Academic sinecure in which to relax

definitions.meaning: a light-duty professorship, a chair that is easy

explanation.surface: A cushy university post as a place to put your feet up.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic chair is a professorship; an undemanding one is a sinecure, and the phrase is also a comfortable armchair.

clue.text: People watching us love? Very possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A question whether onlookers are watching a couple's love.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyeurs are people who watch others, especially intimately, so they are people watching.

clue.text: A dose of fizz with fish?

indicators.note: fizz suggests effervescence, the letters bubbling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dose of fizzy medicine alongside their fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizz' looks like part of the medicine but is the anagram signal for A DOSE OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish is one kind of marine food, so it is an example of the broader term.

clue.text: Artist is second and friend is outside

indicators.note: outside means the friend's word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An artist is ranked second and his friend is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: See 1
Party in contravention of the law?

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A question whether a party breaks the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'of the law?' nods to unlicensed raves, which British law has targeted; it is a link that adds to the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large all-night dance party, a type of party.

clue.text: Is it after 5 that one should call?

indicators.note: after means the pair of words follow the numeral in the answer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether five o'clock is the right time to phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to the Roman numeral, not to another clue or a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a visit, so the noun call is a synonym.

clue.text: Spirit with series of events that has stabilisers?

parts.note: a fairy is a spirit of folklore
a cycle is a series of events that repeats

explanation.surface: A spirit with a run of experiences that needs steadying.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child's bicycle often carries stabilisers, the British name for training wheels.

clue.text: Lauder has a lot of respect

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: esteem is respect

explanation.surface: A praiser who has plenty of admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Estée Lauder founded the cosmetics company, so her first name pairs with the surname given.

clue.text: See 14 down
Unmethodical student employed returning conservative

indicators.note: returning means the word for employed is read going back

parts.note: used means employed
L is the learner driver's plate, a student
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: An erratic student working for the Conservatives again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' signals the reversal of the word for employed only. L for student comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means random and lacking a plan, a synonym for unsystematic.

clue.text: Right oven — cook in it

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: Advice that the correct oven is the place to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a hop-drying kiln of southern England, an oven in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is a way to cook meat in an oven, so the verb is a kind of cooking.

clue.text: School said to have been absorbed

indicators.note: said signals the school name is heard aloud

parts.note: Eton is the English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A remark about a school that may have taken something in.
explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed has been taken into the body, so eaten matches absorbed in the past participle.

clue.text: Talk to ourselves in part that follows record

indicators.note: that follows means the fragment comes after the record in the answer

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the word ourselves is kept, its tail of four letters cut away

explanation.surface: Talking to ourselves in the part after a record is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk to ourselves' reads as the definition, but only 'Talk' defines; 'in part' cuts LVES from 'ourselves', and 'that follows' sets the rest after the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a spoken or written discussion, so it is a synonym for talk.
